claims.text: The Disha Students' Organisation and Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra organised a protest outside Mumbai University's Kalina campus on October 23, 2026.

Protesters outside Mumbai University demanded the complete withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and fresh elections using previous voter lists.
Protesters outside Mumbai University called for the repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of Election Commissioners.
Dr. Pooja, coordinator of Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra, alleged that the Special Intensive Revision exercise could disenfranchise Muslims, Dalits, Adivasis, and working-class voters.
On May 27, 2026, the Supreme Court of India upheld the validity of the Special Intensive Revision exercise conducted in Bihar.

Election Commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote separate letters to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29 objecting to a revised work allocation order issued by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg.

The Cabinet Secretariat declined to intervene in the Election Commissioners' complaint, stating that the letters were sent in an individual capacity rather than as a formal communication from the Election Commission as a whole.
Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg issued the work reallocation order while filling in for Deputy Election Commissioner (Administration) Bhanu Prakash Yeturu while Yeturu was on leave.
The work reallocation order issued by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg was never implemented following objections from Election Commissioners.
Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu is a former Uttarakhand chief secretary who holds an MBBS, a Master of Arts in History, and a law degree.
Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi is a former Haryana chief secretary and former Union Personnel Secretary who holds a PhD in International Economics.
A Cabinet note prepared on August 3, 2026, initially proposed seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's opinion regarding the Election Commissioners' complaint against Maneesh Garg.
The Delhi High Court dismissed a petition by student leader Neha Bora challenging a notice from a special executive magistrate directing her to furnish a bond to maintain peace.

Neha Bora, president of the All India Students' Association, was detained on October 16, 2026, during a protest near Barakhamba Road demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The special executive magistrate's notice directed Neha Bora to furnish a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with a surety.
Protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the handling of the special intensive revision of electoral rolls have taken place in Delhi and across India since October 2.

Indo-Tibetan Border Police Director General Shatrujeet Kapur stated publicly that Indian and Chinese troops have been engaged in ongoing face-offs at several locations along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh.
Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that the border situation gets disturbed when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns.
The Ministry of Home Affairs allocated Rs 400 crore for the modernisation of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, with 70% earmarked for upgrading drone warfare capabilities.
Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera called on the Indian government to send an all-party delegation to Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh to verify whether Chinese forces have encroached on Indian territory.
Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera stated that India's trade deficit with China has ballooned to $113 billion.
Tensions and several face-offs occurred between Indian and Chinese troops near Taksing in Upper Subansiri district of Arunachal Pradesh during July and August.
India and China held their first round of military commanders' talks in the eastern sector in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and 7.
Chinese President Xi Jinping advocated for a dual-track approach to bilateral relations and border issues during his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The Indo-Tibetan Border Police guards the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control between India and China.
In July, Chinese PLA troops pitched tents approximately 6 to 7 kilometers inside India's perception of the Line of Actual Control near Maja after an initial confrontation.
China claims a large portion of Arunachal Pradesh as 'South Tibet' and officially refers to the state as Zangnan.
The Indo-Tibetan Border Police posted video footage of DG Shatrujeet Kapur's speech on social media on Thursday night before later deleting it.
